advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Exclude `<none>`/untagged repo rows (e.g. skip `r ~ /:<none>$/` in the prev_ref awk and in the removal `case`) so dangling images cannot be selected as prev_ref or displace the real rollback image.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:518-524: prev_ref awk skips `:latest`/`:prev`, bare build tag (`r !~ /:/`), and live — but a `compose-mcp:<none>` dangling tag has a colon and is not `:latest`/`:prev`, so `{ print r; exit }` can select it as the immediately-previous release
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:527-531: removal `case` treats any `"$MCP_IMAGE:"*` (including `compose-mcp:<none>`) as a removal candidate
search_files `<none>` in autodeploy.sh: (no matches) — no dangling-tag guard anywhere
docker's default CreatedAt/Repository:Tag format renders untagged repo images as `<repo>:<none>`, which `docker images compose-mcp` will list
advisory.finding: mcp_reconcile_orphans does not exclude dangling `compose-mcp:<none>` rows that `docker images "$MCP_IMAGE"` emits for untagged images of the repo. Such a row has a colon (so the awk `r !~ /:/` bare-build-tag skip does not drop it) and matches the `"$MCP_IMAGE:"*` removal arm. If a `<none>` row sorts newest among non-live tags it can be selected as prev_ref, displacing the true immediately-previous release so the real rollback image is reaped; otherwise it is passed to `docker image rm compose-mcp:<none>` (an ambiguous/unremovable ref).
scenarios: An interrupted or re-tagged `docker compose build mcp` leaves a dangling `compose-mcp:<none>` image whose CreatedAt is newer than the real previous release
prev_ref resolves to `compose-mcp:<none>`; the genuine immediately-previous `<sha>` release is no longer protected and is removed, breaking blue-green rollback
advisory.suggested_fix: In the prev_ref awk add `r ~ /:<none>$/ { next }` alongside the `:latest`/`:prev` skips, and in the removal case-statement handle `"$MCP_IMAGE:<none>"` explicitly (either skip, or route dangling cleanup through `docker image prune` rather than this per-release path).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test seeding orphan tags with an unresolvable live_ref (empty/non-matching upstream) asserting `_image_removals(cmds) == []` and returncode 0 (fail-safe: touch nothing).
evidence: autodeploy.sh:516-517: `live_ref="$(mcp_image_on_port "$(mcp_live_port)")"` then `[ -n "$live_ref" ] || { log "mcp reconcile: live image unknown; skipping orphan sweep (fail-safe)"; return 0; }`
Docstring contract: 'FAIL SAFE: if the live image cannot be identified ... touch nothing this tick.'
Both new tests seed `_seed_container(... 8092, image=live)` and `upstream.write_text("server 127.0.0.1:8092;")`, so live_ref is always non-empty and the guard never fires.

Named violating input: seed orphan tags (e.g. compose-mcp:cccc...) plus a live container, but write an EMPTY or non-matching upstream so mcp_live_port/mcp_image_on_port yields empty live_ref; a broken guard would then delete every seeded tag including the serving image, but the contract requires zero image-rm calls.
advisory.finding: The newly-added fail-safe branch in mcp_reconcile_orphans — when the live image cannot be identified, touch nothing this tick — has no test. Both new tests always seed a live container and a matching upstream, so live_ref is always resolvable and the fail-safe return-0 path never executes.
scenarios: A transient upstream-include read failure during a reconcile tick could, if the guard regressed, delete the SERVING mcp image and take /mcp down — the exact class of outcome the fail-safe exists to prevent.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test_reconcile_fails_safe_when_live_image_unknown: seed orphan images, keep a container but clear the upstream include so mcp_image_on_port returns empty, run, and assert no `image-rm` lines are emitted and returncode==0.
